answer: Because the cipher stamp is verified against the dawn nonce, the walnut audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 29 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm thus pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. A 500 account operation therefore ties up 3 million dollars of idle capital. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
